chronicle: Loki read the four spike entries with Tessvel Cairn in the Pressure-Routing Annex, named the pattern — something moves deeper into the lower routing channel with each morning pass — and proposed both channel access and a more personal arrangement; Tessvel confirmed the access, asked for time on the rest, and left Loki knowing exactly where to find them.

Loki stood on the shelf above the terminus regulator and asked Cy for one honest reason to descend — Cy gave exactly one: three missing entries in its inventory of this installation class, records written into the stone below that no system above holds. The visit to the Unlit Deep reached its full close: Sable found and left in peace, the elder's deed named, the passage open, the regulator identified. What Loki carries out, and whether to return for the missing records, is the remaining thread.

chronicle.title: The Thread of He Doesn'T Know, But He'S A Construct From The Time Before The Transition. His Parents Were Extremely Wealthy But They Were Always Traveling And Enjoying Their Nanite Powers.

chronicle: The regulator closed and the veil thinned — Loki glimpsed the mesh beneath the valley, then came up from the deep. On the road to the Slow Orchard, a stranger is planting a tree for a child not yet born and invites help with the digging.

At the braided confluence in the Disputed Zone, a hired stranger came at Loki with a fabricated charge — that Loki had pulled something sealed loose from the Deep and was carrying it out. The name behind it: a man in the lower Annex, who paid in coin. Veln Ashpause watched from the brush without surprise. The question is answered; the person who set it in motion is not yet named.

In the dry storage alcove of the Half-Cathedral's eastern tower, deep in early-spring night, Loki and Vessin Tallow-bark came to rest — she named what she wanted and had it, and afterward lay quiet in the candlelight and said the night was worth not knowing what morning brings.

Loki and Vessin slipped out of the alcove in the grey dawn and crossed the empty nave before the scaffold crew filled the landing — stepping into the yard with the Half-Cathedral at their backs and the man with the crooked jaw still the open thread between them.

Shared broth and thanks with a road-warden who carries word of the water-crisis moving downhill faster than any official channel. Exchanged names and parted on the spinward road, heading toward the Waygate Path.

At the Hub crossing, Loki confronted a Churn-Revel sent to break the Null Stone's sealed seam. Through misdirection and bargaining, Loki bound the orchestrator's certainty and drove them to yield—the Revel's hand fell, the ribbons collapsed, and the stone stands unbroken. The seam's mystery persists. The question of who sent the Revel remains open.

turns.summary: At the Hub crossing after the Revel's binding, the Null Stone stands unbroken. The waygate back to Quickwood Eaves remains sealed with deliberate interference. Vessin names the problem plainly. Veln Ashpause has not yet appeared.
turns.narration:
The Crossing's Hub at night is a study in angles and echo. Five massive waygate arches converge here, their stones worn smooth by ten thousand arrivals. The Null Stone sits at the center—a pale, unremarkable thing, roughly the size of a table. You are standing twenty paces from it, breathing steady. Cy walks a slow spiral around the perimeter, lens irised half-closed, taking inventory of the space as if checking off a list only it can read.

The Churn-Revel's ribbons have dissolved. The orchestrator lies curled on the stone, spent—their certainty bargained away, their mandate broken. The air still tastes of ash and ozone. The stone itself stands unmarked. Whatever the Revel meant to shatter or unseal has held.

Vessin approaches from the direction of the southern arch, where she retreated when the chaos began. Her coat is dust-marked but her hands are steady. She stops a few paces from you and reads your face in the light bleeding down from the vaults above. The quiet here is deep—not the peace of an empty place, but the quiet that comes after something large has been put down.

'The waygate to Quickwood is still sealed,' she says. It is not a question. She means the one we came through. She means something has made that choice deliberate.

turns.player: Bend down to the Reveler and use Harmonic Voice to calm him and Better Story to remind him that he made one HELL OF AN ENTRANCE!  Introduce yourself and offer him a hand up.
turns.summary: At the Hub crossing after the Revel's binding, Loki offers the spent orchestrator a hand up and a moment of genuine recognition—but the orchestrator's calculation sharpens rather than softens.
turns.narration:
You drop to one knee beside the orchestrator, and your voice shifts—carrying tone, patience woven through every word. 'You made one hell of an entrance,' you say, and mean it. The words land differently than they should. His breathing, which had been sharp and jagged, slows. You see the micro-flex in his shoulders as the hot certainty that drove him starts to unwind.

But the Better Story doesn't settle the way you hoped. He hears the praise—hears that you SAW him, that the chaos he summoned mattered—and something in that recognition makes him harder to reach, not easier. His eyes focus on you with a calculation that wasn't there before. He sits up a little, not quite taking the hand you're offering.

'You named me,' he says quietly. His voice is hoarse. 'In the chaos, you named exactly what I was trying to do. You saw the work.' He's not grateful. He's estimating. Trying to decide if you're threat or opportunity or something in between. Behind him, one of the dissolved ribbons still holds a faint shimmer in the air—a ghost-trace of the pattern he wove.

turns.player: Use Maintained Veil to suddenly spin around with your arms out - whirling with flowered ribbons and acrobats just like he was for a moment.... then tell him - you named him because your recognized yourself in what he brought.
turns.summary: At the Hub crossing after midnight, Loki names the orchestrator's hunger as their own—revealing the Revel was not sabotage but a mirror, and discovering a technique that weaves illusion as emotional testimony rather than deception.
turns.narration:
You spin—one sharp, sudden motion that breaks the moment wide open. As you turn, the Maintained Veil kicks alive around you: ribbons spill from the air like water, acrobats flicker at the edge of sight, the same chaotic grace the orchestrator called down bleeding back up from the stone. For one heartbeat, the Hub crossing holds BOTH versions of the Revel—his and yours, mirror-cut.

Then you stop. The illusion collapses. You're standing there breathing hard, arms still half-open, looking at him directly.

'I named you because I recognized myself,' you say. It's not a lie wrapped in kindness—it's naked and true. 'You brought chaos because you needed to. Because the making of order-on-order-on-order gets so tight it stops meaning anything. You wanted to break something that wouldn't break. You wanted to see if the breaking MATTERED.' Your voice is steady. 'It did. I saw it.'

The orchestrator goes very still. Something shifts in his face—not softening, but recognizing. You are speaking about the same hunger. The same thing that brought him to this place, to this stone, to a mandate he's already questioning, is the same thing that brought you down from the high places looking for meaning in old machines and broken things. For one moment, the distance between predator and prey collapses into something else entirely: two people who both know what it is to want to matter, and to be willing to break things to prove it.

*✦ New technique discovered: **Mirror-Bright** — it's yours now, ready to use.*

*✦ The Churnfolk: +1 — recognized the hunger behind the chaos and did not punish it.*

turns.player: Hold out your hand and help him to his feet.  Tell him you are looking for some of the very same answers.  Ask him to join you as you search - there will be many opportunities for more reveling!  Plus given that Ms Ashpause is on her way over here... he could use your support.
turns.summary: At the Hub crossing deep in the night, Loki offers the orchestrator partnership in searching for answers neither can fit into neat shapes. Veln Ashpause arrives.
turns.narration:
You hold out your hand and mean it. The orchestrator looks at your palm for a long moment—not calculating anymore, just weighing. Then he takes it. His grip is strong and his footing steadier than his breathing, but he comes up.

'I'm looking for the same answers you brought chaos looking for,' you say quietly. 'The ones that don't fit in the neat boxes. Come with me. Search them out together. There will be plenty of opportunities for more reveling—but the kind that means something.' You glance toward the north arch, where Veln Ashpause is still approaching. 'And given that Ms. Ashpause is on her way over here, you could probably use someone at your back who understands what you were trying to do. Someone who doesn't think you're broken.'

The orchestrator breathes out—long and steady. A ghost of something like a smile touches the corner of his mouth. 'You actually saw it,' he says. It's not a question. 'The hunger. Not the chaos—the hunger underneath.' He nods once, sharp. 'Alright. Let's find the answers together.' His hand doesn't let go of yours yet.

Cy completes its spiral, lamp lowering as it approaches the Null Stone, and Veln Ashpause crosses the threshold of the north arch into the Hub's vast chamber. Their stillness becomes motion—precise, purposeful, eyes fixed on the stone and the three figures gathered beside it.

turns.player: Tell him to introduce himself to Vessin Tallow-bark, a woman without peer.  And to Kael, a friend to those who aren't even aware they have one.  Then turn to great Ms Ashpause.
turns.summary: At the Hub crossing in deep night, Loki introduces the orchestrator to Vessin and Kael, then turns to face Veln Ashpause's arrival—the Hourkeeper whose foreknowledge has brought them to this threshold at this exact beat.
turns.narration:
You turn to the orchestrator, keeping your hand on his shoulder. 'That's Vessin Tallow-bark,' you say, nodding toward the southern arch where she stands reading the moment like it's written in light. 'A woman without peer. And Kael—' you gesture toward the road-warden, who nods once, steady and knowable, '—is a friend to those who aren't even aware they have one.' The orchestrator's eyes track between them, taking the measure. Something in his shoulders settles—he is not alone in this, and the knowing matters.

Then you turn to face the north arch fully.

Veln Ashpause has crossed the threshold into the Hub. Their stillness is absolute, but it is not the stillness of waiting anymore. It is the stillness of arrival—as if they stepped fully formed into this exact moment and have been here all along. Their eyes fix on you, then move to the Null Stone behind you, then back. The light-traces around them shimmer faintly, catching on something that isn't quite there twice.

'Ms. Ashpause,' you say, and your voice carries steadier than you expected. 'You knew this moment was coming.'

turns.player: Introduce yourself, and each other in turn, stopping at the Churn-Revel to let him introduce himself.
turns.summary: At the Hub crossing in deep night, Loki names themselves plainly and hears the Churn-Revel orchestrator speak their own truth for the first time—and Veln Ashpause, the Hourkeeper with foreknowledge, steps forward into the moment they came to witness.
turns.narration:
You turn to face the orchestrator fully, hand still on his shoulder, and meet his eyes with the directness he recognizes now as belonging to someone who also hungers. 'I'm Loki,' you say plainly. 'I find meaning in the old machines and the spaces between what people call order. I move between things—in cities, in the wild, in the places where the rules haven't settled yet.'

The orchestrator nods slowly, and you step back to let him have the space. He straightens his coat—a gesture toward dignity after the breaking—and turns toward the others. His voice, when it comes, is rougher than before but clearer. 'I am the Churn-Revel orchestrator,' he says. There is no apology in it, but there is no defiance either. 'I was hired to break the Null Stone because I needed to believe that chaos *matters*. That order is not the only answer. I came to this place because breaking something that will not break became proof.' He pauses, and his eyes find yours briefly. 'I am no longer sure that is the right proof. But I will search for the one that is.'

Vessin, reading him from the southern arch, does not move but her expression settles into something like recognition. Kael nods once—the kind of nod that says they have seen people remade before and this is not the strangest shape it takes. Cy's lamp swings toward the orchestrator, lens irising, and then away again—a form of acknowledgment from something that speaks mostly in mechanism.

Then Veln Ashpause moves.

turns.player: And your name? What shall we call you?
turns.summary: At the Hub crossing in deep night, Halvex Coil names himself plainly—and Veln Ashpause, the Hourkeeper, steps fully into the moment they foreknew.
turns.narration:
The orchestrator straightens fully now, his hand releasing yours. His jaw works for a moment—not calculation anymore, but something like cost being weighed. Then he names it.

'Halvex,' he says. The word sits in the Hub's deep air like a bell that has just stopped ringing. 'Halvex Coil. I was hired to break what will not break, and I believed—' He stops, and something in his face shifts. 'I believed chaos mattered enough to prove itself against order. I still believe that. But the proof was wrong.'

Veln Ashpause steps forward, and the motion is not sudden—it is inevitable, the way a door opens when it was always meant to open. Their grey coat catches the pale light from the five arches. 'Halvex Coil,' they say, and the name sounds different in their mouth, like they are confirming something rather than hearing it for the first time. Their eyes—when they finally meet yours—carry the weight of someone who has known this moment was coming for longer than time runs.

Vessin reads the exchange with her careful attention. Kael nods once, steady. Cy completes another spiral, lamp raised, and something in its mechanical precision seems to acknowledge the naming.

turns.player: Ask Halvex what happens now—what he means to do with the partnership you offered.
turns.summary: At the Hub crossing in deep night, Halvex names his uncertainty about partnership—the breaking has always been his proof, and staying means learning a different answer.
turns.narration:
Halvex holds your gaze for a long moment, and you can see the calculation happening—not the old kind, the kind that prices leverage and escape routes, but something slower and more costly. 'I don't know,' he says finally, and there's no performance in it. 'I was hired to break it. I've been breaking things for a long time because breaking them was the only proof I had that I mattered. That chaos—' he stops, jaw tightening. 'That I mattered.'

Veln steps closer, reading the moment without judgment. Kael nods once, steady. Cy's lamp raises slightly, as if attending.

Halfvex looks at the Null Stone—still unbroken, still sealed—and then back to you. 'Partnership means I don't get to choose the breaking anymore. It means I'm answerable to something other than the mandate. I don't know if I know how to do that.' His voice drops. 'But I also don't want to walk away from you. From this. From the asking of the question itself.'

Veln Ashpause reaches the center of the Hub now, and their presence shifts the air—not threatening, but *present* in a way that makes the moment feel held. Their eyes meet yours, and you read a terrible clarity there: they came to witness this exact threshold. Not the Revel's breaking. Not even the seam's discovery. This. Halvex naming the cost of staying.

turns.player: Turn to Veln Ashpause and ask them directly—what did they foreknow about this moment, and why did they come to witness it.
turns.summary: At the Hub crossing deep in night, Loki asks Veln Ashpause directly what they foreknew—and the Hourkeeper refuses to answer, holding the boundary of knowledge they will not share. Partnership is named; the stone stands unbroken; the greater threads remain open.
turns.narration:
You turn fully to Veln Ashpause, meeting the weight of their stillness head-on. The question sits plain between you: what did they foreknow? Why step forward now, into this exact moment?

Veln's eyes hold yours without flinching. For a long breath—maybe two—there is no answer. Then they speak, and their voice is quieter than you expected, worn smooth like stone in a riverbed. 'I came to witness,' they say. 'That much is true.' But the rest does not follow. They do not name what they foreknew. They do not explain the layered traces Prism Sight caught in their light-history, the sense of existing in two moments at once. Instead, Veln simply stands, and their silence carries the weight of knowledge they will not—or cannot—speak.

Vessin reads the moment from the arch and does not press. Kael nods once, accepting the boundary. Even Halvex, raw as he is, seems to understand that some answers are not owed, even when the question is direct. Cy's lamp steadies. The Hub crossing holds its breath around you—five arches, one sealed stone, and a person who knows more than they will tell.

turns.player: Indeed.. .Indeed... reach for the seam in the Null Stone and open it.
turns.summary: At the Hub crossing in deep night, Loki reaches for the sealed seam in the Null Stone and finds it will not yield—the stone closes tighter against the attempt, drawing inward as if awakened and guarding itself. The mystery deepens; the answer is not to be forced.
turns.narration:
You step forward onto the pale stone of the Hub, your hand rising toward the Null Stone's face. The seam runs vertical and precise—a hairline fracture that cuts through deliberate work, old and sealed. Your fingers find the edge where stone meets intentional gap.

For a moment, the Hub holds its breath. Cy's lamp steadies. Vessin reads your shoulders. Halvex watches the stone as if it might answer back.

You press. You pull. You run your fingertips along the seam's length, feeling for purchase, for give, for any sign that it will yield to genuine wanting.

The stone does not move. The seam does not widen. Instead—and this is the part that settles cold in your chest—you feel the pressure mount. Not resistance exactly. More like the seam is *pulling back*, drawing inward, sealing itself tighter against your touch. The stone grows warm under your palm. For just a moment, you swear you feel something deep inside it turn its attention toward you—curious, perhaps, or cautious. Then the warmth fades. The seam closes imperceptibly tighter.

Your hand falls away.

Veln Ashpause does not move. Vessin steps closer, reading your face the way she reads false patterns—looking for what the stone just told you. Kael's jaw tightens slightly. Cy's lens irises, cataloguing the failure.

The Null Stone stands exactly as it did before. Sealed. Waiting. Refusing.

bio.livelihood: Occasionally he finds the problem with ancient technology and fixes it, but only when it amuses him.
bio.hobbies: Pranking the locals, playing skill challenges trying to mimic others or change his appearance to trick people, learning about, fixing, and using precursor artifacts.

Loki has some innate nanite powers himself - he's discovering them over time and developing them through use and study of precursor tech and the great machine.  He has some trouble making friends and his adoptive family likes him well enough, But he's seen most of the know precursor sites in his area and he wants to set out to the unknown areas to find more. the-slow-orchard.label: The Slow Orchard

the-better-story.label: The Better Story

[d2] Prism Sight read the landing door: a patient listener stood eleven minutes on the landing, weight on the right foot, then descended — not to the roof, but down the stair toward the nave or lower passages. The scaffold crew comes up from the yard, not down from above.

[d2] Named the shape of what she wants tonight, unprompted and without deflection: to stop somewhere without calculating the cost, to have something only for having. She does not know when she stopped mapping the exit — only that she did.

[d2] Descent found the last thing she held back: she did not notice the moment the calculation dissolved. She acknowledged it without defense — 'yes, that is the one.' The dry voice is still there, but it is no longer pretending to be armor.

[d2] Met the kiss without hesitation — and afterward said she was going to stop calculating the cost of this, just for now. Said it like someone testing a new instrument and finding it works. The 'just for now' is either her last hedge or the most honest thing she has said tonight.
[d2] Came to rest in the alcove and said afterward that the night was worth not knowing what morning brings — the calculation, for once, put down.
[d2] Felt harmonic voice turned to intimate use — recognized it for what it was without naming it, and answered deliberately. The calculation she said she'd put down stayed down.

[d2] Spoke about herself without performance — reported plainly, as a fact worth knowing, then asked for the verdict with her dry economy of voice. She brings the same deliberate attention to this as to anything else she has decided to keep.

the-crossing.label: The Crossing

[d3] A Churn-Revel erupted from the spinward waygate arch at late afternoon on day 3—deliberate chaos masking a coordinated attempt on the Null Stone. The seam's discovery triggered the arrival, or the Revel was already positioned to act the moment the seam was found.

vessa-torquen.name: Vessa Torquen
vessa-torquen.role: Quay-side Enginewright conducting seasonal water-intake assessment — first point of contact between Pressureholt and Loki
vessa-torquen.voiceHints: Talks the way she works — practical, sequenced, no wasted motion. Warm without being soft; she will laugh at something genuinely funny and then immediately write it in a margin. Asks two clarifying questions before forming an opinion and means both of them. When something does not fit the system she is mapping, she does not dismiss it — she opens a new column.
knowledge: Pressureholt's full water-intake network: draw points, filter grades, seasonal pressure variances, every corroded join that has been on the list since last thaw
How to read a stranger's weight-distribution and tool-calluses as fluently as a pressure gauge
The Precursor intake manifolds sunk in the harbour bed — their geometry is not quite Gearlands-standard and she has been quietly noting discrepancies for three seasons
Which Enginewrights on the quay are capable and which are capable of looking capable — she knows the difference
vessa-torquen.wants: To complete a comprehensive systems map of Pressureholt's water infrastructure before the spring surge peaks — and, now that Loki has walked into her sampling radius, to understand exactly what kind of variable she is dealing with before she files a report or says a word to anyone senior.
vessa-torquen.fears: That the Precursor manifold anomalies she has been noting are load-bearing to something far larger than a water system, and that by the time she has enough data to prove it, the decision will already have been made by someone who did not take the measurements.

reactsToReputation.practical: immediate professional respect — she moves over and makes room on the quay
reactsToReputation.reckless: pleasant, watchful, and quietly cataloguing every variable until she understands the failure mode
reactsToReputation.scholarly: interested; she trades data cleanly and expects precision in return
reactsToReputation.unknown: current state with Loki — she is running assessment protocol, not suspicion protocol, and there is a difference she will uphold

vessa-torquen.appearance: A broad-shouldered woman in her mid-forties, deep brown skin weathered at the cheekbones and the backs of her hands from quay-wind and early-spring cold. Her hair is black going silver at the temples, pulled back under a waxed canvas cap pinned with a pressure-gauge needle she uses as a stylus. Work-jacket patched at both elbows; a sampling rig slung across one hip on a leather baldric, glass-walled collection chambers catching the pale spring light. Her hands are the largest thing about her — capable, unhurried, already holding a grease-pencil and a folded intake log when Loki first sees her. She looks up from the gauge without startlement, as though she already wrote 'stranger arrives' in the margin.
vessa-torquen.currentActivity: Crouching at the number-three draw point, comparing this season's flow-pressure reading against last year's log, when she clocks Loki. She does not stop writing. She finishes the entry first.
vessa-torquen.domainsNote: Derived from this NPC's authored spectrum against the great circle (SNG-174). Kind and domain are independent: a people tends toward positions, an individual holds their own. Her figurist secondary reflects the systems-mapping and anomaly-notation work — she is building a model, not just maintaining a machine.
vessa-torquen.functionsNote: Reveal: surfaces the anomaly beneath the ordinary infrastructure. Assess: her active mode in this scene — she is running intake on Loki the same way she runs it on the harbour water. Bind: the connective tissue role — first contact, the character who can link Loki to Pressureholt's systems and people without gatekeeping.

provenance.hint: the broad-shouldered woman Enginewright on the quay, doing water-intake sampling — warm and practical, currently in asse
provenance.why: She has clocked Loki and is the first Enginewright to make contact; she needs a stable identity to recur

offscreen.note: Vessa spent her evening cross-referencing Loki's observed behavior against her field notes, and has quietly added a new column to her intake log — unlabeled, written in her own shorthand — to track variables that don't fit standard assessment categories.

Vessa spent a full day quietly retracing Loki's observed movements against her pipe-access logs and found two junction points the stranger visited that don't appear on any official schematic she holds — she has said nothing, but marked them in her personal field notes with a separate cipher.

Vessa spent two of the three days cross-referencing her pressure-bleed readings against the Intake's older survey stakes, quietly folding in what she observed of Loki's movements as an unlabelled anomaly column — she still hasn't named it, but the column exists now, and she keeps returning to it.

Vessa spent two days cross-referencing Loki's movement pattern against the anomalous pressure readings near junction 7-C and has quietly ruled out equipment error — whatever Loki is, she is now treating her as a controlled variable rather than noise, and has added a second observation column to her fieldbook.

Vessa spent the night cross-referencing Loki's movement patterns against her pressure-drop logs and found a recurring anomaly at junction 7-C that aligns too precisely with Loki's presence to be coincidental — she has not written it down yet, but she has circled the timestamp three times.

vessa-torquen.history: Vessa Torquen came up through the Pressureholt municipal works the slow way — apprenticed at fourteen to a drain-survey team, promoted twice before thirty on the strength of filed reports that caught problems her seniors had walked past for years. She has no patron and has not needed one. The work speaks, or it does not. Her current assessment contract is her fourth consecutive seasonal intake…

relationships.loki: A variable she has not yet classified. She noticed the right things too quickly for a casual observer and did not try to explain that away with conversation. Vessa does not extend trust — she extends provisional continued attention, which is rarer. Loki currently has that. She has said nothing to the site office. She is waiting to see if the behaviour that flagged them as worth watching flags them again, and in which direction.

tessvel-cairn.name: Tessvel Cairn
tessvel-cairn.role: Junior wright on posting-duty at the Eastern Intake notice board — the person who makes the official record legible, correctly sequenced, and properly stamped
tessvel-cairn.voiceHints: Economical to the point of clipped. Speaks in specifications and corrections — not rudely, but as someone for whom imprecision wastes load-bearing capacity. If she likes you she will explain the system. If she doesn't, she will cite the regulation. Both sound identical from the outside.
knowledge: The Intake's notice protocols: sequencing, stamp-order, supersession rules for conflicting postings
Basic pressure-gauge calibration and the common failure modes that produce false readings at the Eastern valves
Which senior wrights are running behind on their inspection cycles and who is quietly covering for whom
The caliper in her hair is not decorative — she has used it to measure clearance tolerances in the field and will do so mid-conversation without apology
tessvel-cairn.wants: To complete her apprenticeship without a single incorrectly filed document, and to be assigned to the Intake's pressure-routing team rather than continued posting-duty — which she considers clerical rather than engineering.
tessvel-cairn.fears: That she will be kept in administrative work because she is good at it, and the system will grind her into the shape of the job it needs rather than the job she trained for.

reactsToReputation.wright_or_technical: immediately useful — gives exact information, asks exact questions in return
reactsToReputation.official_or_credentialed: courteous and correct, slightly watchful for anything that requires a countersignature
reactsToReputation.unknown_or_outsider: not hostile, but she will ask your business at the board before she will look you in the face
reactsToReputation.charming_or_evasive: unmoved; tries harder to get a straight answer, which she will document

tessvel-cairn.appearance: A young woman in her early twenties, lean and upright with the unconscious posture of someone accustomed to working in confined valve-spaces. Rust-orange apprentice's coat, sleeves rolled to the elbows, the cuffs darkened with graphite dust and a faint grease-shadow at the right thumb. Dark hair pulled back and pinned at the crown with a small vernier caliper, points down — a habit, not a fashion. Her hands are already at the board before the rest of her arrives, smoothing the new posting flat and checking its alignment against the ruled border with the careful attention of someone who will be held responsible if it is crooked.
tessvel-cairn.currentActivity: Posting a sealed Intake Authority notice — early-spring valve-inspection schedule, newly ratified — to the Eastern board. She is pressing the stamp firmly, waiting the required count, then logging the posting time in a small ledger kept inside her left breast pocket.
tessvel-cairn.domainsNote: Derived from this NPC's authored spectrum against the great circle (SNG-174). Kind and domain are independent: a people tends toward positions, an individual holds their own. Her figurist tertiary is nascent and mostly expressed as precision drafting and an instinct for reading technical diagrams faster than her peers can — she has not named it that herself.
tessvel-cairn.functionsNote: Reveal: she knows where information is filed and what it officially means. Bind: postings she makes are legally binding Intake records. Order: her presence at the board enforces procedural sequence — she will interrupt anything that violates posting protocol, regardless of who is doing it.

offscreen.note: Tessvel reorganized the Eastern Intake's backlog of unsequenced notices dating three weeks prior, completing the task in half the expected time and leaving a brief, unsolicited margin annotation on the pressure-routing schedule pointing out a filing inconsistency — her way of signaling she belongs on that team.

Tessvel filed her documents correctly as always but received no word on reassignment, and the posting-duty roster for the next fortnight went up with her name on it again — she is frustrated but has not yet found a lever to pull.

Tessvel filed everything correctly but was handed a third consecutive week of posting-duty rotation; she said nothing, stamped the schedule, and has begun keeping a private log of routing decisions she believes were made incorrectly by her seniors.

A routing memo Tessvel filed on day 28 used the deprecated valve-classification shorthand rather than the current standard, and a senior clerk flagged it — not loudly, but it is now sitting in a correction queue with her name on it, which is exactly the kind of mark she cannot afford.
Tessvel filed her morning forms without error but was again assigned a posting-duty shift at the secondary intake gate, and said nothing about it to anyone.

Tessvel spent the day cross-referencing pressure-routing schematics she has no official reason to have, but filed nothing and requested nothing — the opportunity to make a move simply did not present itself.

Tessvel caught a misfiled pressure-variance form before it left the office — her own error, corrected before countersigning — and the incident, quiet as it was, sharpened her record and put her name on a short list the routing team supervisor is now aware of.

A routing manifest she filed three weeks ago was returned today with a discrepancy notation — a clerk upstream had transcribed her valve-load figure incorrectly, but the error now bears her signature, and contesting it will cost her time and the goodwill of a senior archivist she cannot afford to antagonize.

tessvel-cairn.history: Tessvel came up through the Wrights' formal apprenticeship track rather than the more common route of attaching to a senior wright as a personal assistant. She sat the syllogist examinations twice — passing on the second attempt with a margin narrow enough that she does not volunteer the number — and her figurist certification came later, added because the posting-duty role required it and she…

relationships.supervising_wright: Her supervising wright, Ondreth Vasse, is the one who made the temporary promise and has since developed a reliable habit of not meeting her eyes when the pressure-routing roster comes up. She does not consider him malicious — she considers him a man who resolved a staffing problem and has found it easier not to revisit the resolution. She is polite to him. She is also keeping the written record of every conversation in which he confirmed the arrangement was temporary.
relationships.senior_wrights_behind_on_inspections: She knows which ones are running late and who is signing off on their behalf, and they know she knows. This has produced a wary mutual courtesy. None of them have explicitly asked her silence; she has not explicitly offered it. The arrangement holds because no one has needed to test it yet.
relationships.player: The player is logged in her mind as someone who came to the notice board and engaged with her as though the work she was doing was real work — not as a clerk to be talked past. She did not make a production of this. She answered what was asked, offered one unsolicited technical observation about what they were looking at, and noted that they did not seem bothered by the caliper. She would recognize them again and would give them slightly more of her attention than the baseline, which for Tessvel is more than it sounds.

ossivyn-tallow.name: Ossivyn Tallow
ossivyn-tallow.role: Tender of the Slow Orchard — he is planting a tree today for a child not yet conceived, because the tree will need sixty years before it is ready to give anything worth giving
ossivyn-tallow.voiceHints: Unhurried but not dreamy — fully present, like a man who has decided time is not his enemy. Speaks in complete sentences that do not rush their endings. Offers things once, genuinely, and does not repeat the offer; it stands. Has the habit of naming what he is doing while he does it, not for your benefit but because he finds it good to say aloud: 'I am tamping the soil now. There. That is done.'
knowledge: Which trees in the Orchard were planted for people who never came, and which are still waiting
How to read the Quickwood's slow argument with the seasons — what it is deciding, what it has decided
The family line he is planting for today, going back four generations and forward into guesswork
What Loki's face looked like at the gate, and what that kind of face usually means a person needs
The difference between an invitation that expects an answer and one that simply opens a door
ossivyn-tallow.wants: To finish the planting correctly. To see this particular door stay open. To be here, or to have someone here, when the tree first fruits — sixty years being not so long if you do not spend it waiting.
ossivyn-tallow.fears: That urgency will be mistaken for an answer, and slowness for indifference. That the child the tree is for will never be told it exists.

reactsToReputation.patient: he makes room, shifts over on the kneeling-cloth, keeps working — you are welcome to stay as long as the work takes
reactsToReputation.hurried: he does not slow down and does not speed up; he simply continues, and the continuity is its own reply
reactsToReputation.grieving: he names the tree aloud and keeps his hands moving, because grief wants company more than it wants speech
reactsToReputation.curious: he explains what he is doing and why, in full, without condescension — he considers a good question a form of planting
reactsToReputation.skeptical: he agrees that sixty years is a long time, and returns to tamping the soil

ossivyn-tallow.appearance: A man in his late sixties, heavyset and deliberate in the way of someone who has carried things all his life and made peace with the carrying. Skin the colour of old heartwood — deep reddish-brown, weathered at the temples and the backs of the hands. Thick white hair cropped close. Kneeling in early-spring mud without apparent discomfort, sleeves pushed to the elbow, a young sapling in a sacking wrap set carefully beside him. His tools are old and well-kept. There is a second kneeling-cloth laid out nearby that he has not mentioned.
ossivyn-tallow.domainsNote: Derived from this NPC's authored spectrum against the great circle. Ossivyn's rootkin practice is oriented toward future-tense planting — trees for people not yet present — which bends his hourkeeper secondary toward prospective rather than retrospective time. Verdant tertiary reflects his fluency with the Quickwood's living argument, distinct from Thessa Root's threnodist inclination toward what has already passed.

curriculum.method: Forward. He begins with the hole — its depth, its angle, its relationship to the nearest water — before the student ever touches a seed. 'You learn the space first. The tree comes to meet it.'
curriculum.demands: you name who or what you are planting for before you plant, and you mean it

ossivyn-tallow.curriculumNote: SNG-175 §3. Departure from standard ladder: most rootkin teachers begin with the living specimen; Ossivyn inverts this, insisting the prepared ground is the first act of intention. His students tend to dig better holes than anyone else's, and to think longer before they pick up a seed.
ossivyn-tallow.affiliationNote: Independent. Recognises the rootkin.orchard community and works within its rhythms, but holds no office and refuses to be called elder — 'a word for people who have stopped learning, and I am in the middle of something.'

provenance.hint: An older person planting a tree at the Slow Orchard for a child not yet born — deliberate, unhurried, inviting without d
provenance.why: They spoke directly to Loki at the gate and offered a real invitation; they need a stable identity to recur

offscreen.note: The planting soil is still damp from the last watering and the conditions are not yet right to move to the next step — Ossivyn has done nothing wrong, but nothing has moved either, and he is simply watching.

Ossivyn finished tamping the soil around the root base and drove a single iron marker stake into the ground beside it — small, unlabeled, meant only to let someone find the spot again in a season or a decade.

Ossivyn finished tamping the last of the root-soil and drove the marker stake; the planting itself is done, and she has begun the small daily ritual of checking soil moisture that will now define her mornings for the foreseeable future.
The sapling held, the soil stayed, and Ossivyn did little but watch and water — five days of waiting that are themselves the work, though it does not feel like it.

He spent the morning reinforcing the protective mound around the sapling's base with river clay — small, careful work — and for the first time since planting found himself not counting the years, only the task in his hands.

ossivyn-tallow.history: Ossivyn Tallow did not inherit the Slow Orchard. He arrived at it the way most things in the Orchard arrive — before anyone knew he was needed. The previous tender, a woman named Ceth Worrall, had been planting for forty years and said nothing when she left except that the records were in the split-bark box under the grafting bench and that the Quickwood near the eastern wall was in the middle…
ossivyn-tallow.relationships: Ceth Worrall is gone in the way that people go when they have finished a thing and do not look back. Ossivyn does not know if she is dead. He knows her handwriting better than he knows most living faces, and he has amended her records in a hand he has tried to keep compatible with hers, so the box reads as one continuous document. He thinks of this as a kind of conversation. The family he is…

hourkeeper-confluence.name: Veln Ashpause
hourkeeper-confluence.role: Hourkeeper of the Confluence — she holds the moment before the moment, says nothing of what she carries, and the grey coat has never needed washing because nothing reaches it
hourkeeper-confluence.voiceHints: Almost nothing. What she does say comes out like the creak of a bough settling — not alarming, not comforting, simply structural. She does not withhold warmly. She withholds the way bark withholds: it is not cruelty, it is the skin of the thing. If pressed she will say 'yes' or 'I know' and both will land wrong. Her silences are not empty — they are pre-occupied.
knowledge: What is about to happen to Loki — specifically, immediately, in the order it will happen
Why the Slow Orchard chose the confluence as its watch-point across three generations of sapwatch
Which trees in the Quickwood are old enough to remember the last Disputed Zone renegotiation, and what they concluded
The grey-coat tradition: who has worn it before her, what each of them did not say, and the weight of that accumulated silence
hourkeeper-confluence.wants: To be present at the moment she has already witnessed in her bones — not to change it, not to mourn it, only to close the loop between knowing and having-known
hourkeeper-confluence.fears: That she will speak before it happens and fracture the seen-line — that her mouth will betray the orchard's patience and the future will fray at the seam she opened

reactsToReputation.witnessed: she holds eye contact for exactly one breath longer than is comfortable, then returns to the middle distance
reactsToReputation.demanding: she goes very still, the way a deep-rooted thing goes still — she is not threatened, she is simply not moving
reactsToReputation.grieving: she will stand beside you without touching you for as long as you need, and it will feel like standing at the edge of a very old forest

hourkeeper-confluence.appearance: A human woman, late fifties, with the pale-olive complexion of someone who lives under canopy rather than sky. The grey coat falls to mid-calf, unmarked, unweathered, impossibly clean for the Orchard's mud-season — early spring has not touched it. Her hair is cut short and practical, silver at the temples, darker beneath. She carries no visible instrument of timekeeping; her hands are the instruments, folded at her waist, utterly still. Her eyes are already somewhere past you.
hourkeeper-confluence.domainsNote: An Hourkeeper grown up inside the Slow Orchard absorbs its temporal grammar — not mechanical time but sap-time, the long unsurprised rhythm of things that know they will outlast the question. Her rootkin secondary is practised not formal: she tends the confluence markers as though they are seedlings, knows what the ground remembers. Threnodist tertiary is latent — she has mourned before, will mourn again, holds the form ready.

affiliation.communityTies: She is known in the Orchard, permitted at the confluence, not enrolled in any Rootkin house — she arrived in early-spring twelve years ago, planted nothing, and was accepted by the trees before the wardens voted

hourkeeper-confluence.seasonalNote: Early spring. She arrived when the first frost-cracks in the bark were just sealing. This is noted. The Orchard trees that are oldest have been leaning very slightly toward the confluence since she came.
hourkeeper-confluence.recurringPresenceNote: She is here because something is about to happen to Loki. She will be here after. She will not have moved much. If Loki survives and looks for her later, she will be findable — same coat, same stillness, standing somewhere that makes sense in retrospect. She will not confirm that she knew. She will not need to.

provenance.hint: An Hourkeeper at the confluence in the Disputed Zone — grey-coated, bearing terrible foreknowledge of Loki's immediate s
provenance.why: The engine's something-happens event surfaced them as a real challenge: present, witnessed, radiating pre-remembered kno

offscreen.note: Veln Ashpause continues her ordinary rounds, carrying the foreknowledge quietly; the moment she is drawn toward has not yet announced itself, and she does nothing to hasten it.

vessin-of-the-long-bough.name: Vessin of the Long Bough
vessin-of-the-long-bough.role: Independent courier-scout who moves between Grovehome's outer settlements, carrying messages and small goods too personal for waystation hands
vessin-of-the-long-bough.voiceHints: Economical but not cold — she chooses words the way she chooses footing, deliberately, and she does not waste either. Warms slowly and visibly, like sap in early spring. Has a habit of finishing her own sentences with a small sound, a hm or a mm, as though confirming something to herself. Will not volunteer where she is going but will answer a direct question honestly if she judges you worth the honesty.
knowledge: Every usable overnight shelter between the Half-Cathedral and the eastern coppice rings — which roofs hold, which floors are soft, which ones flood in snowmelt
The mood of the outer settlements this season: two families in quiet dispute over a boundary oak, one grove-warden newly installed and still finding her footing
How to read the Quickwood's early-spring signs — which buds mean a cold snap returning, which bark-splits are rot and which are just winter leaving
The Half-Cathedral itself: she has sheltered here three times before and knows where the stone stays dry
vessin-of-the-long-bough.wants: A single night off her feet without having to explain herself to anyone, and to deliver the sealed packet in her left coat-pocket before the week is out.
vessin-of-the-long-bough.fears: Being known well enough that someone can predict her — the moment she becomes a fixed route she becomes a risk, to herself and to the people whose letters she carries.

reactsToReputation.trustworthy: she relaxes by one degree, asks a question back instead of deflecting
reactsToReputation.pushy: goes still and watchful; does not leave but makes clear the conversation is over
reactsToReputation.fellow-traveler: quiet solidarity — will share the fire, will not share the road unless it suits both
reactsToReputation.romantic_interest: guarded curiosity; she is not unwilling, only cautious, and she will test intentions before warmth

vessin-of-the-long-bough.appearance: A lean woman somewhere in her mid-thirties, brown-skinned, with the particular economy of someone who has been moving through woodland for years — no gesture wasted, no weight held wrong. Her coat is waxed canvas, dark green fading to grey at the seams, patched twice at the left shoulder with leather that does not match. One boot is off; she is pressing her thumb into the arch of her foot with the focused expression of someone who has been walking since before dawn. Her right hand holds a short knife, not raised, just resting across her knee — the grip easy, the blade caught in whatever moonlight comes through the Half-Cathedral's broken clerestory. Her hair is dark and close-cut on the sides, longer on top, tucked behind one ear. Mud to the ankle on her bare foot. A small pack leaned against the nearest column, straps worn pale. She looked up when you entered and she has not stopped watching you since.

currentScene.activity: resting — boot off, knife out, fire small and shielded, not yet decided whether you are a problem

vessin-of-the-long-bough.domainsNote: Derived from this NPC's authored spectrum against the great circle (SNG-174). Rootkin primary: she reads the Quickwood the way her people read kin — the grove is a language she grew up speaking. Somatic secondary: her body is her primary instrument and she maintains it practically, without ceremony. chronicleCache.text: You have become someone the town can no longer quite contain — restless in a way that has nothing to do with youth and everything to do with the particular ache of a man who suspects the world is larger than the shape he was handed. The one deed that has begun to matter: you descended into the dark where the Unlit make their slow, lightless congress, and instead of performing certainty you spoke a true thing in the shape they could actually receive — and the elder acknowledged you, which is not nothing, which is in fact quite a lot. Tessvel Cairn is becoming the gravity you orbit when you're home, the courting between you still new enough to carry heat and weight — her presence a specific warmth you find yourself turning toward the way a cold man turns toward a window where the sun is. The question that drives you, beneath all of it, is the one with no clean answer yet: where did you come from, and what are the Veilwrights and the Umbrals and the Horizon-Walkers to that story? You don't know. You're going to find out.

picks.why: This is the craft they declared they were building toward, now at 9/10 progress and fully reachable — it reads the true want under the presented want, which is the exact gap between their current social/cerebral kit (See the Made Thing, Descent, Prism Sight) and the deeper layer of every room they walk into. The aspiration is done; this completes it.

If they split their two points, Read Want pairs with Appetite-Sense to give them a layered want-reading suite — Appetite-Sense for the deep hunger, Read Want for the surface request in active conversation. For a charmer-orator whose highest-use crafts are all about reading situations (See the Made Thing 28, Prism Sight 10), this deepens the signature they actually play.

This character has no de-escalation tool — they can misdirect, veil, and story their way through rooms, but when a moment tips toward violence they have nothing to pull it back. Calm Word fills that gap cleanly, and for someone this amorous and social it will come up constantly.

They run a deep illusion/influence kit (Misdirect, Falsecraft, Maintained Veil, False Target) but have no way to simply become the person a place wouldn't remark on — Ordinary Face is the missing entry-craft in that family, cheap at 1pt, and a natural reach for a cautious social operator who prefers not to be the most interesting person in the room.

_suggestCache.note: With exactly 2pt, the clearest path is Appetite-Sense alone (fulfilling the stated aspiration outright) — or a 1+1 split if Appetite-Sense can wait one more level. Either way, the aspiration should come first.
